newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks ended at their day's high as an already bouyant bourse got a late shot in the arm from U.S. employment data and a perception Wall Street is set to rise, dealers said on Friday.

However, after the close of local trade U.S. analysts began predicting a drop on Wall Street as bonds began to be sold off on the March jobs report which showed average hourly earnings were higher than expected.
But local traders said they were starting to become less troubled by the choppy waters on the New York markets that have sent damaging ripples around global financial markets.
South African shares kicked off Friday by ignoring an overnight fall on the Dow and went on to firmly hold their gains all day.
The all-share index added 34.7 points to 7,015.8 as the industrials index puts on 36.8 points to 8,239.1.
Volumes were healthy and most blue chips posted modest gains as Johnnic rose 25 cents to 59.25 rand, SAB put on 150 cents 137.50 rand and Anglo gained 375 cents to 273.00 rand.
"It was not a bad day's trade. We got a late boost from the U.S. data," said one dealer.

Next week dealers and portfolio managers are expecting a flat performance South African shares even if the Dow endures another rocky time. They say the local market will seek to break away from Wall Street's stranglehold.

There are some encouraging signs that people are starting to look at the fundamentals. Our market is not as overvalued as Wall Street and so should behave differently," said Andre Joubert, portfolio manager at Investec Asset Management.
Dealers said Friday saw good demand from both local institutions and foreign players as the sell-off earlier in the week left some shares looking cheap.

The gold index had a dull day, lurking around in negative territory for almost the entire session, but the late rally in the rest of the market had a knock-on effect and pulled the index into the positive at the end.
The golds index edged up 2.3 points to 1,291.3.
The shares have come under pressure recently from a renewed bout of weakness in the ailing bullion price which has been suffering from a falling silver price.
On Friday the yellow metal struggled to hold value as the silver sell-off continued and it remained exposed to a test of the $345.00 an ounce limit.
South African share futures drifted through the day, also seeking to ignore trends in New York.
The all-share contract was last at 6,442/58 from 6,393 as the industrials was at 8,025/35 from 7,975. The golds contract was at 898/920 from 906.
